office_does: The assessor values every taxable property in Grant County each year for property taxes; levy rates are set by the taxing districts and voters.
race_blurb: Open seat after Assessor Melissa McKnight did not seek re-election. Clayton Johnson, the office's sales analyst running without a party preference, was alone on the primary ballot; Republican Anson Bartrand reached the general as a declared write-in who cleared the 1% primary threshold.

candidates.summary: Nine-year Grant County Assessor's Office appraiser and sales analyst, running without a party preference on integrity, transparency and fair valuations.
highlights: Commercial/industrial appraiser and sales analyst in the assessor's office for nine years [S1]
Would track staff-owned properties and bar staff from appraisals where they have a personal or financial interest [S2]
Says assessments should be 'entirely free of politics' and runs as a non-partisan [S2]

experience.basis: Runs on nine years inside the assessor's office as appraiser and analyst, though he has never held elected office.

candidates.summary: Republican precinct committee officer and CFO of a land investment company, 25, who reached the general ballot as a write-in from the primary.
highlights: Filed as a declared Republican write-in in July and cleared the 1% primary threshold [S4][S6]
Pledges to reduce unnecessary spending and complete assessments on statutory deadlines [S1]
CFO of Sentinel Shores, LLC; accounting degree from CWU and law school at the University of Idaho [S1]

experience.basis: 25-year-old first-time candidate from outside the assessor's office whose public roles are party precinct and executive-board posts.

spending.basis: Statement pledges to find responsible ways to reduce unnecessary spending and to be a careful steward of taxpayers' money.
